about: Per-row source text for the table built from EPR 2016 Schedule 23 Part 3 Table 2. ACTINV does not read this file. Superscripts in row_text are written ^(...).

source.citation: The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1154), Schedule 23 Part 3, Table 2 (Concentration of radionuclides) with Table 3 (secular-equilibrium daughters)
source.edition: legislation.gov.uk data.xml, in force from 2026-07-30, modified 2026-09-07; Tables 1 and 2 substituted 2018-05-02 by SI 2018/428
source.jurisdiction: United Kingdom, England and Wales (Environmental Permitting Regulations)
source.scope: Activity concentration in Bq/g of radionuclides in a solid or relevant liquid, below which the substance is outside the radioactive-substances regime as referred to in paragraphs 5 and 6 of Schedule 23 Part 2; solid-material concentration only (Table 1, the NORM table, and the catch-all row for other radionuclides are not converted). Choosing this table is a regulatory decision for the analyst.

paragraph_texts: The Table 1 referred to in paragraph 4 of Part 2 (NORM industrial activities) is—
The Table 1 summation rule in respect of column 2, 3 or 4 means the sum of the quotients A/B where—
“A” means the concentration of each radionuclide listed in column 1 of Table 1 that is present in the substance or article, and
“B” means the concentration of that radionuclide specified in column 2, 3 or 4 (as appropriate) of Table 1.

The Table 2 referred to in paragraph 5 of Part 2 (processed radionuclides of natural terrestrial or cosmic origin) and paragraph 6 of that Part (radionuclides not of natural terrestrial or cosmic origin) is—
The Table 2 column 2 summation rule means the sum of the quotients A/B where—
“A” means the concentration of each radionuclide listed in column 1 of Table 2 that is present in the substance or article, and
“B” means the concentration of that radionuclide specified in column 2 of Table 2.
Where any radionuclide carries the suffix “+” or “sec” in Table 1 or Table 2—

that radionuclide represents the parent radionuclide in secular equilibrium with the corresponding daughter radionuclides which are identified in column 2 of Table 3 in respect of that parent radionuclide, and

a concentration value given in a table in this Part in respect of such a parent radionuclide is the value for the parent radionuclide alone, but already takes into account the daughter radionuclides present.
The Table 3 referred to in paragraph 3 is—
Figures in Sch. 23 Pt. 3 para. 1(1) Table 1 substituted (2.5.2018) by The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2018 (S.I. 2018/428), reg. 1, Sch. para. 8
Sch. 23 Pt. 3 para. 2(1) Table 2 substituted (2.5.2018) by The Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2018 (S.I. 2018/428), reg. 1, Sch. para. 9

catch_all_row.printed: Any other solid or relevant liquid radionuclide that is not of natural terrestrial or cosmic origin
catch_all_row.alternative: or that concentration which gives rise to a dose to a member of the public of 10 microsieverts per year calculated by reference to the International Atomic Energy Agency publication “Application of the Concepts of Exclusion, Exemption and Clearance”,IAEASafety Standards SeriesNo.RS-G-1.7.
catch_all_row.reason_not_in_table: not a nuclide; the regulation gives 0.01 Bq/g or the concentration that gives 10 microsieverts a year by IAEA RS-G-1.7 for any other artificial radionuclide. ACTINV does not apply it: such nuclides are reported in not_listed.
